paper.title: Good Classification Measures and How to Find Them (NeurIPS 2021)

claim.method: pairwise inconsistency of binary classification measures (Accuracy vs Balanced Accuracy)
claim.dataset: Yandex.Weather rain-prediction confusion matrices, all 12 forecast horizons (bundled in data/meteo)
claim.split: all bundled threshold, day and horizon cases
claim.preprocessing: none; the confusion matrices are counted as given
claim.seedPolicy: deterministic counting; the script calls random.seed(42) but draws no random numbers for this table

metric.name: inconsistency rate of Accuracy vs Balanced Accuracy

adapter.why: The official script prints a matrix of discordant counts and the number of cases, not the percentage in Table 4; the adapter runs it unchanged and divides the two.
adapter.source: Runs the pinned meteo_inversion_matrix.py unchanged with the argument full, from the repository root, and writes 100 x discordant(Acc, BA) / total to JSON. Arguments: --output <artifacts/result.json>.
differences: project-owned adapter, not official repository code
it computes the Table 4 percentage from the two counts the official script prints; the paper does not show this division
the environment is a 2026 Python 3.11 stack; the paper does not state its versions
